memoryText: Now you have been pleased to bless the house of your servant, that it may continue forever before you. For it is you, O LORD, who have blessed, and it is blessed forever.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read 1 Chronicles 17:27 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This is the last line of David’s prayer after God made the covenant with him. It is a prayer of someone who has just been handed an astonishing promise and is still catching his breath.

“Now you have been pleased to bless.” David begins with God’s pleasure. God was not forced to bless. He chose to, and he took pleasure in it. The blessing flowed from his good will. It was not earned.

“The house of your servant.” David calls himself a servant, though he is the king. His house is not a palace of his own making but a household that God has chosen to bless. Notice that God’s promise reached beyond David to his descendants. We are blessed, and so are our children after us.

“That it may continue forever before you.” David asks for the promise to endure. He knows that it will outlast him. The Chronicler wrote these words when there was no king in David’s line on the throne, and so this prayer was an act of hope. The promise had not failed. It was waiting for its fulfillment.

“For it is you, O LORD, who have blessed, and it is blessed forever.” This is the final confidence. The promise rests on the God who made it. David is not bragging about his future. He is resting in God’s word. If God has said it, it will happen.

As a Christian, you can pray this verse with joy. The promise to David is fulfilled in Jesus, and through him we too are blessed forever. When you are tempted to doubt that God will finish what he started, say this verse.
weekInReview: This week you read the heart of David’s story according to the Chronicler. You saw how the Chronicler passes quickly over Saul’s death and gathers all Israel to David. You watched the first attempt to move the ark fail with Uzzah, and the second attempt succeed with joyful music. You read David’s psalm of thanksgiving and God’s great covenant promise: “I will establish his throne forever.” You also saw David’s sin in the census and his choice to fall into the hand of the LORD, whose mercy is great, and his refusal to offer a sacrifice that cost him nothing. Then you read about the careful ordering of the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers. In Psalm 96 and the opening of Psalm 105, you sang the songs David gave to Asaph.
reflectionQuestions: David refused to offer a sacrifice that cost him nothing. What is a cost you are willing to bear for the sake of worship or service?
The promise to David finds its fulfillment in Jesus, the Son of David whose kingdom has no end. How does that give you confidence in God’s promises?
David prepared for a temple that Solomon would build. What are you preparing for the next generation that you may never see completed?
prayerPrompts: Thank God for being pleased to bless his servant.
Thank him for the promise fulfilled in Christ.
